deviation: The draft gives the Customer no ownership of bespoke deliverables. The Supplier keeps all Supplier IP, including improvements and derivatives developed during the Services. The Customer gets only a non-transferable licence limited to the term and conditional on full payment, instead of ownership or a perpetual licence. Arcadia could lose the right to use deliverables it paid for when the agreement ends. This falls below the playbook position and the fallback.
suggested_text: 6.1 Each party retains all rights in intellectual property it owned before the Effective Date or develops independently of this Agreement. The Customer owns all Customer Data and all Deliverables created specifically for the Customer under this Agreement, including all intellectual property rights in them, and the Supplier hereby assigns (and shall procure the assignment of) all such rights to the Customer on creation. 6.2 The Supplier retains ownership of its pre-existing tools, methodologies, software, know-how and templates that are generic and not created specifically for the Customer ("Supplier Tools"). 6.3 The Supplier grants the Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive licence (with the right to sublicense to the Customer's affiliates and service providers) to use, copy and modify the Supplier Tools to the extent embedded in or necessary to use the Deliverables. 6.4 The Customer grants the Supplier a non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to use Customer Data solely to perform the Services for the Customer during the term.
